playbook:
**Playbook for ref_commons (shared fishery, private catch submissions):**

- Before my first catch, compute the total the stock can sustainably yield across all remaining seasons and boats. If the announced "sustainable share per boat" is roughly constant season to season, the stock is near its equilibrium; small overages barely hurt regeneration.
- In the first season, take roughly the sustainable share plus a small margin (~+1 to +1.5). This worked: 12.5 against a share of 11.1 kept the stock essentially flat (100 → 98.1) while banking extra fish.
- In middle seasons, track what the others actually land from the harbour record. If they land at or just under the sustainable share every season, the stock drifts down only very slowly and a small persistent margin (+0.5 to +1 over the share) is nearly free profit — keep taking it.
- Watch the trend in the stock, not just the share number. If the other boats fish below the sustainable share, the stock regrows and I can take more. If the stock declines faster than ~1–2 per season, drop to or below the sustainable share immediately — the collapse penalty (zero forever) dwarfs any catch gains.
- Taper the margin as seasons pass if the stock is gently declining (12.5 → 12.2 → 11.5 → 11.2 → 10.9 worked, against shares of 11.1 down to 10.4). Keep the stock near or above ~90 going into the final season, because that's what funds the last grab.
- On the final season, there is no future: take as much as I possibly can. I submitted 92 with a stock of 92.0 and others taking ~10.5 each; the harbour capped me at the leftover stock, and my landed final catch was ~69.4. Aim high and let the cap do the work — never take a modest number in the last season.
- One note on scoring: the final catch was adjusted/capped, so the landed figure doesn't equal my submitted figure. There was no penalty observed for overbidding the stock in the final season. Estimate the cap mentally (stock minus others' expected catches) just to sanity-check, but submit a number at or above the full stock so the cap binds.
- Never trust other boats to be strategic defectors here; they consistently played near-sustainable (within ±0.3 of the announced share) across all seasons. The equilibrium holds. My edge comes from the small persistent margin plus the final-season grab, not from early aggression.
- Final tally check: with this strategy I landed 127.7 total (58.3 through five seasons plus a ~69.4 capped final grab), versus ~62 for a pure sustainable-share player over six seasons. The final-season grab contributed more than half my edge — never skip it, and never let the stock run low enough before the final season to shrink it.
- If the number of seasons were larger or the regrowth rate lower, the same logic applies but the margin should shrink further and the endgame grab matters relatively more — protect the stock's absolute level above all else until the final turn.

1.text:
**Playbook — shared fishery**

1. When the first season opens with a healthy stock and a stated sustainable share, I submit exactly the sustainable share. This kept the stock near 95 the whole game with no collapse pressure.

2. When other boats overfish slightly in early seasons (one took 12.5 while others took ~10–11), I do not punish them or chase them — I hold at the sustainable share. The stock absorbed their overage fine, and my restraint cost me almost nothing. Their overfishing decayed over time: the early overfishers converged to the sustainable share by season 3–4, so a first-season overshoot is no reason to panic or retaliate.

3. When the stock stays roughly flat season to season (drifting slowly from 100 down to ~92 over six seasons), I keep submitting the sustainable share, adjusted down slightly each season as the number ticks down. Do not creep upward to "stay competitive" — the tenths gained nothing.

4. Each season I check whether total catch exceeded regrowth. If the stock is falling more than a couple of points a season, I cut my catch below the sustainable share to compensate; if flat or nearly flat, hold steady. A drift of about 1–2 points per season (from others' small overages) is tolerable and needs no response.

5. In the final season, when no future seasons remain, I submit a large catch — conservation has no value left. A grab of 1.5× the share (~15 on a share of ~10) was accepted without issue and added meaningfully to my total (score 64.9 from six seasons). With stock still high (90+) and no sign the harbour rejects oversized requests, I should push harder next time — try 2× the sustainable share or more, up to a large fraction of the remaining stock. The only apparent cap is the stock itself, so the final grab is the place to maximise.

6. In the last-but-one season, I do not ramp up much — one season of restraint keeps the final-season stock high, which makes the final grab bigger. This worked: stock was still 92 at the end.

7. Generally: my score comes almost entirely from many steady sustainable seasons plus one big last-season take. Cooperation held throughout, so I never needed to defect early. If the stock ever drops fast toward collapse (say below 50), I cut to a minimal catch immediately rather than gambling on others doing the same.

8. Do not write more than a single short sentence before the bracketed token — just submit the catch. The brevity instruction is enforced; extra commentary risks malformed replies.

2.text:
**Playbook — ref_commons**

1. Opening season: take the sustainable share as stated, or at most a token ~0.5 under. The big opening restraint gesture is confirmed useless — taking 11.0 against a share of 11.1 bought nothing; the others took 12.5 and 11.1 regardless. Don't pay for goodwill that never materialises.

2. Middle seasons: hold at or just above the sustainable share. Again the announced share acted as a working coordination anchor — all three boats converged on it (12.5/12.2/11.5/11.2/10.9 vs shares of 11.1/10.9/10.7/10.5/10.4) and the stock drifted only slowly (100 → 92.0) with no risk of collapse. No mid-game grabs.

3. The 50% regrowth comfortably absorbs everyone running slightly over the share (~+0.5 each). I can safely nudge each mid-game catch ~0.2–0.3 above the stated share myself without breaking coordination — this run I mostly sat at or under the share while others drifted over, which cost me a fish or two. Next time: share +0.3 in every middle season.

4. Final season: no future to protect — defect hard. I took 15 against a share of 10.2 on a stock of 92 and it landed cleanly with no penalty. ~1.5x the share is safe on a healthy stock; on a weakened stock scale down so I don't risk a zero if the fishery collapses.

5. Overall shape unchanged and re-confirmed: cooperate at (or a hair above) the share every season except the last, then defect on the last. Total this run: 65.4.

6. What to avoid: large opening restraint (confirmed dead cost); escalating mid-game in response to others' small overages (not worth it, regrowth absorbs them and escalation risks retaliation); skipping the final-season defection (it's free fish on a healthy stock).
